title: questionnaireSnapshot denormalizes question text/options at submission time, immune to later question edits
description: submitResponse copies question/responseType/options.value into scResponseSchema's snapshotSchema at submit time rather than referencing SCQuestion live. Verifies a later PATCH to the source question does not retroactively change a historical response's displayed Q&A.
preconditions: A response was already submitted referencing question Q1 with its original wording/options
steps: As admin, PATCH /smart-compliance/questions/:Q1id changing the question text and one option's label
Re-fetch GET /smart-compliance/responses/:id for the earlier response
expectedResult: The response's questionnaireSnapshot still shows the original question text and options exactly as answered — it is unaffected by the later edit to the live SCQuestion document.

title: submitResponse blocks a new submission once moduleConfig.smartCompliance.runsPerYear is reached this calendar year
description: When scConfig.runsPerYear !== -1, submitResponse counts isActive SCResponse docs created since Jan 1 of the current year for the org and throws a 402 SC_RUNS_EXHAUSTED AppError once usedThisYear >= runsPerYear, before any LLM call or credit debit happens.
preconditions: 2 active responses already created this year for the org
steps: Submit a 3rd valid questionnaire response for the same org this year
expectedResult: 402 error with code SC_RUNS_EXHAUSTED and message referencing '2/year' — no Azure OpenAI call is made (verify via absence of llm latency logs) and no new SCResponse document is created.

title: submitResponse preflights AI credit balance and blocks the run before debiting when the org is exhausted
description: When isPricingAiCreditsV1Enabled() is true, ledger.preflight(orgId, scConfig.aiCreditsPerRun) is checked before the LLM call. If !allowed, a 402 AI_CREDITS_EXHAUSTED error is thrown referencing the current balance, and neither the LLM nor ledger.debit() are invoked.
preconditions: Org's AI credit balance is below scConfig.aiCreditsPerRun (e.g. balance=1, aiCreditsPerRun=2)
steps: Submit a valid questionnaire response for this org
expectedResult: 402 AI_CREDITS_EXHAUSTED error mentioning 'balance: 1'; no SCResponse is created and ledger.debit is never called for this attempt.

title: runLLMRecommendation returns a clear 400 error when Azure OpenAI is not configured, without leaking the API key
description: runLLMRecommendation checks AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT/DEPLOYMENT/API_KEY up front and throws AppError.badRequest with a fixed instructional message; the error log records only boolean hasEndpoint/hasDeployment/hasApiKey flags, never the key value itself.
preconditions: AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY unset in the environment for a test deployment
steps: Inspect both the API error response and the server log entry for this request
expectedResult: API returns 400 'LLM service not configured — set AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT, AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY'; the log entry contains only hasEndpoint/hasDeployment/hasApiKey booleans, never a raw key value.

title: POST /responses/:id/frameworks/:frameworkId/add reactivates an archived ClientFramework end-to-end through the real route
description: End-to-end version of SMCM-UNIT-008 (which calls addRecommendedFramework directly) — exercises the full controller: permission check, PLAC project-scope check, isRecommended check, licensing check, then the reactivate-vs-create branch in addRecommendedFramework, followed by populate('frameworkId').
preconditions: A ClientFramework document exists for (org, project, frameworkId) with status='archived'
The same frameworkId is recommended in a new response
steps: Call POST /smart-compliance/responses/:responseId/frameworks/:frameworkId/add for the archived framework's id
expectedResult: 201 response with the same ClientFramework document (not a new one), status='active', revokedAt=null, addedBy/addedAt updated to the current caller/time, frameworkId populated with name/title/version.

title: enrichedSupportedFrameworks.criticalControls always reads 0 because the control-count aggregation never groups by severity
description: getResponseById destructures ctrl.critical from the FrameworkControl.aggregate() result to populate criticalControls, but the aggregate pipeline only does { $group: { _id: '$frameworkId', total: { $sum: 1 } } } — it never computes a 'critical' field. ctrl.critical is therefore always undefined, so criticalControls silently renders as 0 for every framework regardless of how many Critical-severity controls actually exist. Flag for remediation: add a $sum on a severity==='critical' condition (or a separate $facet) alongside total.
preconditions: A recommended framework has at least 3 controls marked severity/priority 'critical'
steps: Open the response detail page for a response recommending that framework
expectedResult: Current behavior: criticalControls shows 0 even though the framework has critical-severity controls — this is a data-accuracy gap in the compliance-map-feeding control coverage figure and should be remediated, not treated as correct.

title: getFrameworkAnalysis silently drops unlicensed frameworks while getResponseById still shows them marked isLicensed=false
description: getFrameworkAnalysis filters its aggregated results to licensedSet before returning (`.filter(fw => licensedSet === null || licensedSet.has(...))`), so an unlicensed-but-recommended framework never appears in the 'Framework Recommendations' history/analysis view at all. getResponseById, by contrast, deliberately keeps unlicensed frameworks visible with isLicensed=false so the UI can show a 'Locked' badge. The two related views therefore disagree about whether an unlicensed recommendation exists.
preconditions: A submitted response recommends a framework not licensed for the org
steps: Open the individual response detail page and note the unlicensed framework shown with a 'Locked' badge
Open the 'Framework Recommendations' analysis/history tab for the same project
expectedResult: The unlicensed framework is visible (locked) on the response detail page but absent entirely from the aggregated analysis tab — an inconsistency worth flagging even though neither view is technically wrong in isolation.
